summary.headline: Harsha Engineers Q4 FY26 Engineering EBITDA rose to INR77 crore; FY26 Engineering revenue INR1,444 crore, guided to double-digit FY27 growth.
summary.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 consolidated Engineering revenue of INR382 crore and EBITDA of INR77 crore, versus adjusted EBITDA of INR64.3 crore in Q3 and INR66 crore in Q4 FY25. For FY26, Engineering revenue grew to INR1,444 crore from INR1,269 crore, with consolidated EBITDA of INR264 crore (about INR270 crore adjusted for the new Labour Code impact). Solar revenue was INR183 crore with PAT of INR10.2 crore. Management guided to double-digit FY27 consolidated growth, with India Engineering in the mid-teens, and to maintaining current margins. The call also covered weak Romania profitability, the Advantek ramp-up, and the China steel-cage expansion.

segments.name: Bearing cages (India Engineering)
segments.commentary: India-to-India cage business grew about 11% in FY26 per management. Large-size cages grew about 14% to about INR49 crore, with mid-teens to 15-20% growth expected.

segments.name: Bushings
segments.commentary: Revenue INR127 crore in FY26, up about 25%, driven by design conversion in wind planetary gearboxes from bearings to bushings. Management targets 25-30% growth in FY27.

segments.name: Stampings
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR60 crore. Growth drivers are AC compressor components and white goods. Management expects at least 20% growth next year and 15-20% mid-term.

segments.name: Solar
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR183 crore with PAT INR10.2 crore. Q4 revenue about INR91 crore, roughly doubled YoY. Management expects more than 25% growth and Solar EBITDA margin to hold near the FY26 level.

segments.name: Advantek (India, subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Still at low utilisation; FY26 EBITDA INR4 crore but net loss about INR11 crore on depreciation and interest. Sales expected to grow at least 3x in FY27; current installed capacity seen generating INR250-300 crore turnover.

segments.name: China subsidiary
segments.commentary: FY26 turnover about INR120 crore, PAT about INR5 crore profit. Brownfield steel-cage expansion to be commissioned in H2 FY28; INR70 crore capex in FY27 and INR20 crore in FY28.

segments.name: Romania subsidiary
segments.commentary: FY26 turnover about INR247 crore with PAT loss about INR14 crore. Cage share of mix at about 22%, targeted to rise to 30-35%. Wind market in Europe not yet recovered.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth expected to be double-digit, with India Engineering in the mid-teens; India growth described as high-teens to mid-teens in the Q&A.
Management expects to at least maintain current margin profile in FY27, with an aim to improve it.
Over 2-3 years, management expects consolidated EBITDA to rise 100-200 basis points; India Engineering EBITDA has been consistently about 20%.
Maintenance capex in India of INR30-40 crore in FY27 and a similar amount in FY28; China expansion capex of about INR70 crore in FY27 and INR20 crore in FY28.
Advantek subsidiary expected to reach peak with current installed capacity in about two years; a second-phase capex plan is to be finalised in the next few weeks, with work starting this year.
Management indicated the India-level business could reach INR2,400-2,500 crore and consolidated INR2,700-3,000 crore on current capabilities, depending on capacity additions.
capex_capacity: Harsha has three facilities in India (the third, at Bhayla, commissioned in FY26), one in Romania and one in China.

Advantek is in its first year of operations and running at low utilisation; its sales are expected to grow at least 3x in FY27. Second-phase Advantek capex is being firmed up for additional capacity in key growth verticals.
China brownfield steel-cage expansion has begun; it will add steel cages to a predominantly brass-based portfolio, with commissioning in H2 FY28.
Management said the Advantek capex includes infrastructure that will not translate immediately into fixed-asset-to-revenue multiples.
Saket Kapoor noted PP&E closing balance of about INR615 crore.
demand_pricing: Export growth of about 17% in FY26 was attributed to improving European and US industrial markets; US import tariff on cages was cut to zero, aiding US picks-up.

Pass-through of raw-material costs (steel, brass, metal prices) to customers is contractual, with an average lag of about four months. Q4 growth was mainly volume-driven, as metal prices moved mainly from late December to February/March.

Europe demand is improving slowly, but management said there is no definitive recovery and that cost and pricing issues remain. Europe is about 30% of sales, China just over 10%, US 6-7% and Japan about 2%.
Domestic bearing makers are ramping capacity and are expected to invest further; management is bullish, though it flagged risks from the war and petroleum prices.
Cost pressure is building from oils, lubricants and plastic cage material; logistics has not been impacted so far. Management is working to mitigate or pass through these costs.
Management said wallet share is about 70-90% in India but only 10-20% with large overseas customers and 2-3% with the Japan-based customer.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q4 revenue growth came from pricing versus volume, and was commodity inflation fully passed through?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 27% consolidated growth was mainly Solar; Engineering grew 15.7% YoY. Growth was mostly volume-led, and pass-through is automatic with an average lag of about four months.

qa_highlights.question: What were the absolute FY26 revenue and PBT figures for the China and Romania subsidiaries?
qa_highlights.answer: China: turnover about INR120 crore with PAT about INR5 crore profit. Romania: turnover about INR247 crore with PAT loss about INR14 crore. Combined subsidiary loss was INR9 crore after correction; management said losses would reduce significantly.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Europe demand and restructuring?
qa_highlights.answer: Europe is slowly improving, with no sharp recovery. Restructuring is ongoing, the cost structure is not yet right, and Romania still has negative margins. Management is evaluating how long it can sustain these margins.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: India maintenance capex of INR30-40 crore per year; China expansion INR70 crore in FY27 and INR20 crore in FY28; further Advantek phase-two capex is being finalised.

qa_highlights.question: What is Advantek's ramp-up timeline and revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Current installed capacity expected to peak in about two years, with turnover of INR250-300 crore. Expansion beyond that is planned.

qa_highlights.question: What drives bushing growth and what is the stamping outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Bushing growth comes from design conversion in wind planetary gearboxes away from bearings. Stampings (about INR60 crore in FY26) are driven by AC compressor and white goods components; management expects at least 20% growth next year.

risks_watch: Europe recovery is slow and unconfirmed; management has no clear customer read on demand, and Romania still runs negative EBITDA with restructuring incomplete.
Input cost pressure from oils, lubricants and plastic cage material; pass-through lags about four months, so near-term margins could be squeezed.
Advantek: low utilisation, FY26 net loss about INR11 crore on depreciation and interest; second-phase capex plan to be finalised in the next few weeks and its size not yet disclosed.
Subsidiary loss figures were corrected on the call (INR9 crore vs INR11 crore, Advantek INR11.4 crore vs INR11.5 crore); verify against the annual report.
Geographic mix and Solar growth (about 100% in Q4) drove the headline 27% growth; track Engineering-only growth (15.7%) against the mid-teens FY27 guidance.
Macro risks flagged by management: the war and petroleum prices could affect domestic bearing-maker demand in the short term.
key_quotes: And on your questions for the pass -through mechanism, yes, it is very well-established pass-through mechanism with the customer.
So, we are very bullish. There could be impact of, you know, current war and petroleum prices and all that.
So, last whole year, we are seeing demand has slowly improved over the year.
We are continuing to face massive inflationary pressure in Europe, which is also adding to this whole challenge.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on India Engineering, bushings, large-size cages and domestic bearing-maker demand, and gave specific FY27 growth targets. It was more cautious on Europe and Romania, saying the recovery is slow, there is no definitive turnaround, and restructuring is incomplete; on margins it said it would maintain them, with improvement as an aim rather than a firm target.

adds.what: China brownfield steel-cage expansion (adds steel cages to brass-based portfolio)
Advantek second-phase capacity in key growth verticals (capex being finalised, work to start this year)

growth.why: Management guides FY27 consolidated revenue growth to double-digit (India Engineering mid-teens, Bushings 25-30%, Solar >25%, Advantek sales at least 3x), backed by the Bhayla plant commissioned in FY26 and the Advantek and China expansions, though most new capacity is H2 FY28 or unspecified and the backing is partly specific.
